plan.framing: Adopt the harness with these adaptations.

items.change: Add a type checker for the main dynamic language in check mode, with a baseline so existing code passes and new code is checked; point the typecheck layer at it and record the baseline as a dated deferral.
items.why: Dynamic code without a checker lets an agent's type mistakes through every static layer.
details: main dynamic language: python (236203 source lines); suggested checker: mypy or Pyright

items.change: Write the project's non-standard practices as rules in AGENTS.md, and fill docs/ARCHITECTURE.md by hand: the harness placeholder check passes generic template text (maideps/ai-harness-framework#23).
items.why: Agents follow written rules; unwritten local conventions are exactly what they get wrong (arXiv 2602.11988).
details: README: README.rst; contributing: none; architecture: none; decision records: 0; conventions: none
stated rules: 0 in 0 files
agent context files (presence alone scores nothing): none

items.change: Run the verification layers under the declared legacy runtime (a container or a pinned toolchain in CI), separately from the harness's own Node 18 or later, and keep agents away from runtime-sensitive code paths without that toolchain.
items.why: Code verified on a different runtime than it ships on is not verified.
details: python 2.7 (setup.py, classifier): cycle 2.7 end-of-life since 2020-01-01

items.change: Declare each verification layer command explicitly in package.json scripts (for example phpunit, bin/rails test, make check), so no required layer reports only SKIP.
items.why: The harness picks layer commands from root markers; when it does not detect the repository's main language, its layers run the wrong tool or SKIP, and a SKIP-only required layer fails verify-feature (D-029).
details: the harness would detect none, but the main language is python

notes: merge commits are excluded
renames are not followed, so a renamed file's history starts at the rename

files are those tracked at HEAD; content is read from the working tree
line and byte counts come from the built-in counter
a file is binary when its first 8000 bytes contain a NUL byte, as git decides
vendored: any path segment in node_modules, bower_components, vendor, vendors, third_party, third-party, thirdparty, Pods
generated: lock files, *.min.js, *.min.css and *.map
symlinks and submodules are never followed
paths are those tracked at HEAD; vendored paths are ignored
test files are matched by name and directory conventions; tests are never run
build-tool test runners (Maven, Gradle, Rails minitest, RSpec, go test, cargo test) count when tests sit beside the build file
files under test and fixture directories, and src/<set>/resources, are not classified as documentation

type checkers are found by config file; inherited tsconfig settings (extends) are not followed

manifests are files tracked at HEAD outside vendored directories, read as text; setup.py and build files are never executed
nothing is installed or resolved; versions are as declared
for a version range, the lowest declared version is assessed
runtimes declared under test or fixture directories are marked testFixture and do not count as the product's runtime
end-of-life dates come from the table as of 2026-10-21; a runtime is end-of-life on or after its cycle's date
